spectra.caption: Getting here, as one scroll-driven trip: the plane lands, the metro brakes into Thaltej Gam, a taxi does the last 2 km, and the building lights up.
About. The building is the prism: a white beam hits it and splits into art, science, technology, your senses and you. Move the cursor and the light bends.

shivasva.caption: A section of the home page. The design is the client's; the backend, CMS and deployment behind it are mine.
Projects like Shivdhara Swarnim come out of the admin CMS. The client adds and edits their own projects, without calling me.
Brahmdhara Residency, another project. Each one is run from the same CMS, with its own pictures, address and details.
The contact form. You pick what the enquiry is about, and it goes to the client's email and into a Google Sheet.

sorted.caption: Client pick on a product shoot: 300 picked from 3,424 photos across 56 products. Every product gets its own row, so picking for a client is a scroll, not a folder hunt.
The products view. Every shot of the same product is grouped together, with how many photos and angles it has.
Every number on the site was measured on one machine, a 2020 MacBook Air with the base M1. 3,677 photos off one camera were searchable in 10 minutes 42 seconds.
From the shoot disk to the client's Drive the same night. Pick a person or a category, paste the client's Drive folder link, and it uploads straight from the SSD.
Between the disk and the delivery there are five steps: plug in, index, search, people, export. The disk is only read, never written to, and nothing leaves the Mac until you export.

cravache.caption: A brief lands on the desk, from a khaman house this time, with its fee, its patience and what it will cost you in sleep. You run the whole agency from screens like this one.

deepdive.caption: The page. 150K+ marketers, founders and operators, fed every day by one server.
The grid. Every cover is a headline the machine wrote, over a clip from the ad it is picking apart.
The blog. One long read a day on why an ad worked. I don't write it. I wrote the thing that writes it.
Inside a post: the one number that matters, set as a card, then the story in short sections.
The front page. A new teardown lands every day, whether I show up or not.
The newsprint look. One number, set big: 7.89M people watching GTA VI launch at the same time.
The poster look. Headline up top in Deepdive blue, the takeaway underneath.
The terminal look, for the tech stories. Dated, headlined, done.

sportified.caption: The victory reel, rendered here from sample match data. Six seconds built from the score alone: winner, score, scorers, player of the match. No broadcast footage.
A player of the match card in the grass theme the whole page moved to. Sample render.
The group leaders board in the same theme. Sample render.

vibe-raas-led.caption: One of the eight visuals. It is drawn live, not a video on loop, and it moves with the music because the software listens to the mixer.
The patterns are drawn from Gujarati textile and folk motifs and built by hand, eight visuals in four colourways.
The Vibe Tribe logo on the stripes visual. One laptop drives all three walls, the 50 ft stage screen and the two side screens, and it works with no internet.
The control app on a phone. Pick the screens, the visual and the colours; the BPM comes off the mixer.

vibe-raas-tickets.caption: The pass the buyer gets: the night, the venue, how many passes and a QR code. No buyer name on it, because passes get forwarded.
A phone at a pickup point. Hold up the QR, or type the six-letter code. The bottom line counts what has been handed over.
Green: nothing collected yet. Pick how many passes to hand over and tap the big button. Demo Buyer is made up; this is the real code on a demo database.
Handed over. The phone saves it at once and syncs when it has signal.
Amber: part of this order was already picked up. It shows how many are left and where the rest went.
Red: every pass on this QR is already collected, and it says where and when. A second scan stops here.

clapper.caption: The landing page at clapper.in, scrolled top to bottom: the hero, the shot log writing itself, how it works, and the free guides for whoever holds the phone on set.

fitkit.caption: Today, on test data. Tonight's bedtime up top, then how rested you are, last night's sleep and the day's effort.
Sleep, on test data. Last night against what the body needed, with deep, REM and light set against a typical range.
Why the readiness score is what it is, on test data. Every line is measured against your own usual, not an average person.
Train, on test data. It asks how hard the session felt and plans the next one around it.
Body, on test data. Resting heart rate, HRV and blood oxygen, each set against your own usual range.
